description.en-US: Apps that manage network and device connections
Apps that change how the device works

description.com.buran.wifinotifier:
Wi-Fi Notifier does exactly one thing: it tells you the name of the Wi-Fi
network your phone has connected to. There is no screen at all - the app lives
in the notification shade.

One silent notification that always shows the network the phone is on right now,
with a Stop action that shuts the watcher down. If the name is hidden, it also
carries one tap straight to the screen that unhides it.

An earlier version posted a second, alerting notification on every new
connection. It is switched off for now - the silent one already carries the name
and no sound is wanted - but the code is kept, so it can return later as an
opt-in switch.

Once a name has been read, the app keeps showing it while you stay on that
network, even if location is switched off afterwards; joining another network
asks for the switch again.

On the first launch the app asks for three permissions: notifications, nearby
Wi-Fi devices and location. Location is not used to determine your position:
Android classifies the name of the connected Wi-Fi network as location data and
reports "<unknown ssid>" without that permission. The watcher is a foreground
service typed location for the same reason - a "while in use" location
permission keeps working for a background service only when the service is
declared as a location service.

The app has no network access, no analytics, no advertising and no third-party
libraries: it builds against the Android SDK alone.

whatsNew.com.buran.wifinotifier:
One notification instead of two.

* The separate "Wi-Fi connected" alert is switched off: the silent ongoing
  notification already shows the network name and updates as soon as it
  changes, so a second notification was only clutter. The alert code is kept
  in the app, so it can return later as an opt-in switch.
* The ongoing notification still carries the Stop action and, when the name is
  hidden, the one-tap action that opens the screen which unhides it.
